q1: SELECT EMAIL AS EMAIL FROM PERSON GROUP BY EMAIL HAVING COUNT(EMAIL) >1
q2: SELECT EMAIL FROM (SELECT EMAIL, COUNT(*) AS COUNTER FROM PERSON GROUP BY 1 HAVING COUNTER > 1) AS A
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT EMAIL AS EMAIL FROM PERSON GROUP BY EMAIL HAVING COUNT(EMAIL) >1
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT EMAIL FROM (SELECT EMAIL, COUNT(*) AS COUNTER FROM PERSON GROUP BY 1 HAVING COUNTER > 1) AS A
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not semantically equivalent. Q1 returns distinct email addresses that appear more than once in the PERSON table. Q2, however, returns one row per email address with a count greater than 1, which means it returns one row for each such email (not distinct email values). The difference arises from the structure of the queries, specifically how grouping and subquery output are handled.
counterexample_dsp: A test database with duplicate emails will show Q1 returning one email (distinct) and Q2 returning one row per email (same email repeated).
